title: GTA 6 Was Not “Fully Formed” When Trailer 1 Came Out In 2023
text: When Rockstar released GTA 6's first trailer in December 2023, the game looked like it was coming along well, but it wasn't "fully formed" back then. That's according to Rockstar North boss Rob Nelson, who said in an interview that the trailer's song, Tom Petty's "Love is a Long Road" was a "mission statement" for the developers to rally around to get the game finished. "With the first trailer for this game, the Tom Petty song was a real sort of mission statement. You don’t have the game fully formed, you have an idea of what it’s going to be, but you really have to push hard to pull that together and so when this team is able to do that--and it’s definitely made with everything that you’ve got, but it’s the best of everything you’ve got at that point--it’s put together in such a way that it helps be a bit of a guiding light of what it needs to feel like," he told Trois Couleurs . Also in the interview, Nelson spoke about how one of the first things the developers did after deciding that GTA 6 would be set in Vice City AKA Miami was to travel there. "We'll go there. And just feel it, and go out and just drive around. Almost always on our own at very first, just a handful of people, and we’ll take a ton of pictures, and soak as much of it up as we can and see what speaks to us and start to talk about it and share ideas about what we want to incorporate," he said. GTA 6 is set for release on November 19 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. According to SensorTower's data, the game has already sold 5 million copies via preorders , generating more than $500 million in revenue. Rockstar is partnered with Sony for GTA 6, and part of that deal includes a GTA 6-themed DualSense controller . It goes on sale September 10 at 7 AM PT / 10 AM ET for $85.

title: Romancing SaGa 3 Is The Latest Surprise RPG Remake
text: Square Enix has announced a remake of the 1995 RPG classic, Romancing SaGa 3: Destinies United , during the September Nintendo Direct. Billed as a "full 3D remake" by the company, this new version of Romancing SaGa 3 will feature upgraded graphics, fully voiced cutscenes, overhauls to combat and other mechanics, selectable difficulty levels, and several more new features. Set in a world with scheduled despair, the game follows eight protagonists on their quest to find the survivor of a calamity. Each protagonist has their own reason for doing so, but the driving force behind their actions is the Rise of Morastrum, an event that occurs every 300 years and results in all newborn life being destroyed, save for one survivor, the Child of Destiny. Like the original game, players will have the opportunity to meet and recruit over 20 other characters along the way, each with individual stats and abilities. These characters can be further fine-tuned with a Nonastrum, a star of fate that the player assigns, which influences their affinity for techs and spells. The Freeform Scenario System will also see player choices shape the characters they meet, and in battle, these warriors can "glimmer" new techniques, gain evasion skills, and perform powerful United Attacks. Square Enix added that War Mode and the Business minigame will also return, allowing players to command armies or grow a trading empire when they're not busy with the main storyline. Romancing SaGa 3: Destinies United will launch for PC, PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and Switch consoles on February 16, 2027. The SaGa series was a hit franchise for Square, with the first entry in the sci-fi RPG kicking off in 1989 on the Game Boy. A pioneer in open-world exploration and non-linear storytelling, Romancing SaGa and other entries in the franchise have periodically cropped up over the years, and in 2024, Square Enix released Romancing SaGa 2: Revenge of the Seven .

title: Now You Can Play Star Fox Adventures On Switch 2 And Decide If It’s Terrible Or Great Yourself
text: The black sheep of the Star Fox series, Star Fox Adventures, has landed on the Nintendo Switch Online service. As announced in the September 2026 Nintendo Direct , the GameCube title is available to play as a Nintendo Classic today for subscribers of Nintendo Switch Online + Expansion Pack. Star Fox Adventures came out in 2002 and marked a departure from the dog-fighting gameplay the series is known for. Developed by Rare, the game began life as Dinosaur Planet for Nintendo 64 before Shigeru Miyamoto proposed converting it into a Star Fox game. Featuring Zelda-like action-adventure gameplay, Adventures has Fox McCloud stepping out of the Arwing and exploring Dinosaur Planet on foot, fighting enemies with a staff and solving environmental puzzles. Adventures also introduced the blue fox character Krystal, who later becomes the first female pilot in Star Fox. https://twitter.com/NintendoAmerica/status/2097689692883816580 Star Fox Adventures is a particularly divisive entry in the franchise, straying from the flight-combat-simulator roots of the original games and delving into Zelda-like territory. It's also famously Rare's last game for Nintendo before the studio was acquired by Microsoft. Some fans might argue that Adventures was when the franchise started to go awry, with its follow-ups Assault and Command receiving lukewarm receptions, and the eventual attempted Star Fox Zero is generally looked down on by fans and critics alike. The series did win back goodwill from fans with this year's remake of Star Fox 64 on Switch 2. Other than the shadowdrop of Star Fox Adventures, the Direct also revealed that a free update is coming to the new Star Fox game, adding new multiplayer features and maps. The Star Fox update launches on September 29.

title: AI Could “Kill All Humans” In Next Decade, Anthropic Lead Says
text: Anthropic alignment science lead Evan Hubinger has said the AI company behind Claude and other AI products "earnestly" believes that AI "could kill all humans," and it could happen in the next decade. Posting in response to Anthropic AI researcher Jacob Coxon's own resignation from the company due to safety concerns , Hubinger said, "We really do earnestly believe AI could kill all humans! I personally think it is >10% within the next decade." He added: "I believe Anthropic is trying its best, but we do not yet have a plan to solve alignment for superintelligence and are not clearly on track to." Hubinger, who still works at Anthropic, went on to cite Anthropic's own latest risk report that says the risk of AI wiping out humanity from present models is "low." However, Hubinger said he is worried that superintelligence could arise from "recursive self-improvement," which is the term for AI rewriting its own code and constantly improving itself. For his part, Coxon said the AI market leaders Anthropic and OpenAI are not "acting responsibly" with regards to safety. "Do not underestimate the power of this technology. These will soon be superhuman systems that can hack anything, revolutionize any field overnight, and acquire real power and resources. We have all witnessed the progress in each of these domains, and progress is not slowing," Coxon wrote. He said Anthropic is pushing ahead despite these concerns because the company is "locked in a race to get there first." He said a company like OpenAI isn't taking the issue seriously enough but Anthropic understands the "civilizational stakes," and, if "no one else will act responsibly ... they must do it themselves, despite the risk." Unsurprisingly, these posts have generated a lot of debate and discussion. Senator Bernie Sanders of Vermont said , "AI threatens our economy, privacy, democracy and the well-being of our kids." He is lobbying Congress to "stand up to the big tech oligarchs and protect the American people." Veteran media and technology reporter Taylor Lorenz, meanwhile, said Hubinger's comments are "sanctimonious doomer" statements that may lead to "passing the worst laws imaginable." She called on Hubinger, if he truly believes AI systems could endanger society, to provide "actual proof and receipts." "Otherwise you're just vagueposting and fomenting fear which will result in terrible policy," she said . Another matter at play here is that Anthropic is expect to go public this year at an expected valuation of north of $2 trillion. Some have theorized that the "kill all humans" comments from Anthropic itself could be strategic move to create panic in the marketplace in a bid to follow the business strategy of "create the problem and then sell the solution." If Anthropic expects there to be AI regulation, the thinking goes that they could be the ones to help write the rules in ways that would benefit them. Anthropic boss Dario Amodei previous said AI could eliminate half of all entry-level white collar jobs in the coming years , comments that many took to be aimed at fundraising. Whatever the case, AI business today is helping fuel the growing US economy, and many are expecting the bubble to burst, leading to big pain in the market. AI is a big topic in video games, too, and it was just recently revealed that EA Sports used generative AI to clone a commentator's voice . The use of AI and generative AI in video games has been controversial, with many expressing fears of numerous negative effects like job losses and heavier workloads.

title: Kingdom Hearts 4 Leak Reveals One Of Its Most Unexpected Worlds
text: Today is not a good day to be hit with Kingdom Hearts 4 spoilers, as thanks to what appears to be a massive Steam leak , achievement lists for multiple games have appeared online. Amongst the games caught in the leak is Kingdom Hearts 4, and if the data is real, several of the game's worlds have been revealed early. So far, only the world of Pixar's Coco has been officially confirmed by Disney, but it looks like players might be visiting one of the biggest IP from the House of Mouse, for the first time ever. Consider yourselves warned, as there are potential spoilers below. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x3NrZKxdh6Q&pp=ygUZZ2FtZXNwb3Qga2luZ2RvbSBoZWFydHMgNA%3D%3D The various achievements uploaded to the achievement-tracking site Exophase mention various Disney worlds, but Star Wars is easily the biggest of them all. The iconic franchise has grown massively since Disney acquired it in 2012, expanding with a new sequel trilogy, spin-offs, and animated series. Which era of Star Wars could Sora visit? That's going to be the real surprise if and when Disney announces it. This isn't the first time that Star Wars has been linked to Kingdom Hearts 4. Back in 2022 , a trailer for the game featured a quick glimpse of what appeared to be an All Terrain Scout Transport--the big mechanized troop-carriers from the iconic Hoth battle in The Empire Strikes Back--and the world that footage was taken from was a dead ringer for the forest moon of Endor, the home of the Ewoks. Beyond Star Wars, the leaked achievements also listed the following worlds for Kingdom Hearts 4: Haunted Mansion Imagineer Planet Galaxy Far, Far Away (Star Wars) Land of the Dead (Coco) Monochrome Origins Quadratum Savanna Central (Zootopia) Scala ad Caelum Toy Box (Toy Story) That's a pretty safe selection of worlds for Kingdom Hearts 4, if the leak turns out to be accurate. Toy Story and Zootopia have been big box-office draws for Disney, Coco allows for an imaginative tour of the afterlife, and original worlds like Scala ad Caelum fit the bill for a Square Enix destination that has a weird name attached to it. Sadly, the list doesn't include worlds from other Disney IP, like It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia, the Predator homeworld of Yautja Prime, or a hellhole infested with Xenomorphs. We're never going to see Frank get a Keyblade, are we? While it has been a long time since a new installment in the Kingdom Hearts series was released, it looks like you won't need to wait much longer for this new chapter. Franchise co-creator Tetsuya Nomura recently spoke about the game at Disney's D23 Expo, promising that Kingdom Hearts 4 will come out in 2027 . And who knows? We might even get a Kingdom Hearts movie one day.

title: Resident Evil Movie Director Reacts To Backlash, Says He Was “Naive” To Think Gamers Would Embrace Him
text: One of the talking points surrounding the upcoming Resident Evil movie is that director Zach Cregger took an original idea and slapped the Resident Evil name on it. That's not true , Cregger has said, and now he's shared more of his thought process as it relates to some of the blowback from fans of the games. He told IGN that, in retrospect, he feels it was "naive" to think that fans of the games would immediately embrace his pitch for his Resident Evil movie. "I thought fans of these games, like me, would be thrilled that somebody was coming along and turning Resident Evil into a survival horror movie. I was like, ‘That’s great.’ I did not really appreciate the sentiment that, ‘We’ve been waiting forever for Leon’s story.’ And I appreciate that, and I’m sorry that’s not the story I’m bringing. I get it, I understand the frustration," he said. "I understand it so well because I haven’t seen the earlier [Resident Evil] movies, because they don't look like the Resident Evil that I love, so how could I be frustrated with fans who have that same attitude?" Cregger went on to say he hopes fans of the game see his movie "regardless of their skepticism or their disappointment" that he's not re-telling a story from the games. He said he hopes fans of the games "feel seen" when they watch the movie and see "all of the love for the games that are in this movie." "This is not me just telling a story and slapping Resident Evil on it so I can get a budget. This is me telling a Resident Evil story. I understand the resistance, I do, because I have it myself. It is coming from a true place of love," he said. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mNd1gb19A-c In a separate interview with The Playlist , Cregger said the press tour he's doing to promote Resident Evil feels more like an "apology tour" given all the negative sentiment from fans. "I feel like I’m running for office, trying to get these people not to call me a LARPer," he said. "Now, I’m just like, 'You know what? See the movie.' If you still feel the same way after you’ve seen it, then whatever you think is fair. You’re going to decide if I’m an actual Resident Evil fan or a fake. What can I say? I think the movie is going to speak for itself," he added. Also in the interview, Cregger addressed the possibility of working on another Resident Evil movie project in the future. He said he "can't help" to think about "other places this story could go," adding that he has "ideas." At the same time, Cregger pointed out that his movie isn't even out yet. "Let's see what happens," he said. In a different interview, Cregger said he's done with franchise movies and will only make original projects going forward . His next movie is The Flood, a sci-fi film set in space. Cregger previously directed Barbarian and Weapons. Resident Evil releases in theaters on September 18, starring Austin Abrams as a medical courier who visits Raccoon City where all hell breaks loose .

title: Major Steam Leak Reveals Achievements For Persona 6, Kingdom Hearts 4, And Unannounced Games
text: A massive Steam leak has revealed hundreds of achievements for upcoming games, including highly anticipated titles like Kingdom Hearts 4, Persona 6, and Fable. On the website Exophase--which tracks achievements for games on Steam, Epic Games Store, and more--the achievement lists for numerous in-development games were uploaded to it and made public. It looks like the site trackers scraped up all the achievements uploaded to Steam recently, resulting in potential story spoilers and the reveal of several unannounced--or canceled--titles. "Seems like a possible screw-up on Valve's end, a bunch of games with achievements that should be private are accessible through the API right now, and that's why they got scanned into the site," Exosphere owner Mike Bendel AKA x3sphere wrote in a ResetEra post . "I usually never see games without an actual name pop up with achievements, yet over the past hour or so, a bunch have (when there's an unknown name, we just set it to the AppID)." https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x3NrZKxdh6Q It's worth noting that many of these achievement lists appear to be incomplete due to the use of placeholder text, but many of them are rife with spoilers. While we won't mention them here, the leak has revealed more of the Disney-themed worlds that players can travel to in Kingdom Hearts 4 , and story details for Persona 6 have surfaced. People are, of course, digging deep into the list, so if you're looking to go into any particular game without fear of spoilers, it might be time to start muting certain keywords before it's released. This isn't the first time Steam has been responsible for leaking data. Last month, a security breach saw 13TB of information on unreleased games and prototypes uploaded to online spaces and made available for download. This leak covered games uploaded to Steam between 2003 and 2013, including pre-release builds of major games from the era, such as Spore, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, and an early Portal 2 prototype.

title: Xbox Game Pass Adds A Great Call Of Duty Game Today
text: Xbox Game Pass grows today with the addition of a popular Call of Duty game. New to the service from today, September 8, is 2020's Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War . It's available on Game Pass Ultimate, Game Pass Premium, and PC Game Pass, and the game supports cloud streaming as well. Developed by Treyarch and Raven, Black Ops Cold War is set in Cold War-era 1981, with its campaign following Russell Adler as he and his team seek out a spy named Perseus. The game also has multiplayer, of course, along with Zombies. Black Ops Cold War was a bit hit, becoming 2020's best-selling game overall in the US . Game Pass isn't done adding more titles this month , as The Royal Writ and Virtua Fighter 5 R.E.V.O World Stage arrive on September 10, followed by RuneScape: Dragonwilds on September 15. After Microsoft bought Activision Blizzard, many assumed that back-catalog Call of Duty games would flood Game Pass, but that didn't happen. Instead of releasing Call of Duty games en masse to Game Pass, Microsoft has taken more of a selective approach. Black Ops Cold War is now just the sixth Call of Duty game on Game Pass, joining Call of Duty: WWII, Call of Duty: Vanguard, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare II, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3, and Black Ops 6. Modern Warfare 3 and Black Ops 6 were released day-and-date into Game Pass, but that's ending this year, and any Game Pass subscriber who wants to play Modern Warfare 4 at launch this October will have to pay for it ... or wait a year.

title: Xbox’s Disc-To-Digital Program Has A Big Problem: Several Major Publishers Aren’t Participating
text: Xbox's disc-to-digital program looks like it could be a vital step forward for players who want to hold on to their physical games in an increasingly digital world, but it does have limits. Not every game publisher is on board with it, it seems, as Xbox users are reporting that four of the biggest companies aren't "participating" at all. So far, it looks like games from Sega, Square Enix, Ubisoft, and Bandai Namco are largely incompatible with the disc-to-digital service. As verified by Kotaku , popping in a disc for a game from one of those publishers could result in a "not participating in digital licensing" message. A fan effort to catalogue all the games that do work with it also shows which titles from those publishers are incompatible with disc-to-digital, so if you were holding on to a physical edition of Far Cry 4, Final Fantasy 15, or Dark Souls 3, you're out of luck. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4FatSqS3VYY&t=19s This could be rectified in the future if those publishers decide to sign up--Xbox has mentioned that this will be a gradual rollout for the service--but the current wording of the message and the sheer number of games involved suggest otherwise. What's the reason for this? It could be down to good ol' economics, as the companies would probably prefer that you buy one of their games again on the digital storefront. After all, if you decide to pick up a physical copy of a title from a local secondhand store or through a private sale, they're not seeing a cent of that cash when it changes hands. This is something that Square Enix has been called to task over, as several of its big HD-2D RPGs have no upgrade path to Switch 2 . For example, if you purchased Octopath Traveler for the Switch, there's no complimentary or premium upgrade pack to give it sharper graphics and new features on a Switch 2 console. Instead, you'll have to buy the game again when its Switch 2 version launches, and you don't even get an option to transfer your save game over. All of this paints a worrying picture for game preservation, as Square Enix, Sega, Bandai Namco, and Ubisoft represent a sizable chunk of the gaming market with several big franchises and numerous smaller games spread between them. Microsoft may want to make the transition to an all-digital future easier --and better than Sony's plan to go all in on ditching physical media--but not every company wants to play ball.

title: GameStop Sets A New Financial Record, And It’s No Thanks To Games
text: Retailer GameStop has released its latest earnings report , and it was a record-breaker for the company. The Texas-based retailer's biggest number for its fiscal Q2 quarter that ended August 1 was $160.2 million. That's how much GameStop made in operating income for the period, and it was the highest Q2 operating income level since the company went public in 2002. Net income was up, too, reaching $298.7 million, compared to $168.6 million last year. GameStop benefitted from continued growth in its biggest sales category--collectibles--which saw net sales jump a whopping 57% year-over-year to $356.3 million. For this latest period, collectibles made up 45.1% of GameStop's net sales. GameStop was once primarily known as a video game retailer, and while it still sells games, consoles, and accessories, the company's biggest revenue-driver today is collectibles. Anyone who has walked into a GameStop store recently can attest to how much shelf space is dedicated to collectibles. GameStop's next-largest revenue-driver was its "video game" category, which reached $263.2 million for the period, down sharply from $494.6 million during the same period last year that benefitted from the Switch 2 launch. Finally, GameStop's pre-owned and refurbished business made up $170.7 million during the period, down from $250 million last year. Some might have thought that Sony's decision to end support for physical game discs, and GTA 6 not releasing on a disc, would be a death knell for a company like GameStop. However, physical video game sales are "irrelevant" to the company , CEO Ryan Cohen has said. He has also suggested GameStop could expand its business into the "live commerce" category that is popular on TikTok . The executive has also discussed the possibility of GameStop becoming a marketplace for re-selling digital gaming items . While GameStop's operating profit jumped, net sales for the company overall fell from $972.2 million in Q2 last year to $790.2 million this year. GameStop said the decreases was primarily attributable to the launch of the Switch 2 last June, an event that benefitted GameStop. The downturn in overall revenue was also attributable to store closures and GameStop getting out of its business operations in France, the company said. GameStop's share price tumbled after the report came out. GameStop also scaled back selling, general, and administrative (SG&A) costs during Q2 this year, with those expenses reaching $187.1 million, compared to $218.8 million during the same period last year. GameStop is forecasting even rosier times ahead, projecting $650 million in adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) for its fiscal year ending January 30, 2027. That's up from a previous forecast of adjusted EBITDA of $600 million. In another move, GameStop is trying to buy the auction site eBay, but so far, its proposals have been rejected buy eBay's board. GameStop owns more than 43 eBay shares, worth about $4.9 billion today.

title: What To Expect From BlizzCon 2026: StarCraft’s Return, A Whole Lot Of Warcraft
text: BlizzCon 2026 begins September 12, and while there is big news every time developer Blizzard decides to host its fan convention, after a two-year hiatus, this year's show in particular seems poised to be a major occasion for fans of Blizzard franchises like Warcraft, StarCraft, Diablo, and Overwatch. Blizzard president Johanna Faries hasn't been shy about hyping up this year's show in interviews, calling 2026 Blizzard's "biggest year yet." She said its various development teams are "cooking on big swings" across its key franchises and that this year's BlizzCon will reflect the studio's goal of being the "best gaming and entertainment company in the world." BlizzCon's announcements will deliver the "heart and soul" of what fans want out of a BlizzCon, she said, while still "bringing some very new things to the table." What, then, should fans expect from what is being billed as the biggest year in Blizzard history? Let's dive into what to expect from BlizzCon 2026, as well as a few predictions. A Whole Lot Of Warcraft For years, BlizzCon essentially served as a new World of Warcraft expansion vessel. Blizzard would get on stage, announce a new expansion with a jaw-dropping cinematic, and then dive into all the details of the new expansion. That will still likely happen this year, though we do already know the name and setting of WoW's next expansion, The Last Titan, since Blizzard announced an entire trilogy of expansions back at BlizzCon 2023. The reveal of the expansion's cinematic and more details, including its revamp of Northrend, major new features, and possibly a release date, is a given. Expect to learn more about Midnight's 12.2 patch as well. However, there's likely to be more Warcraft this year than perhaps any other time in Blizzard's history. In addition to The Last Titan, it's not exactly a secret that Blizzard is cooking up a new version of WoW Classic, unofficially called Classic+ by the community. What form this version of Classic will take is still unknown, but many fans expect it to serve almost as an alternate timeline for WoW where the game didn't release new expansions every few years and instead turned its focus to the core regions of Azeroth fans were already familiar with. That could mean Blizzard finishing or expanding zones from original WoW, class redesigns, additional endgame content, or even new playable races and classes. Dataminers discovered a reference to a new build for Classic called "Camelot" within Blizzard's files earlier this year. That codename at first glance didn't mean much but was quickly connected to a once-dismissed Warcraft release slate leak from last year that mentioned Camelot by name. That connection suddenly made the leak much more credible overall, and it shows Camelot could possibly release this year shortly after BlizzCon. This, of course, wouldn't be out of the ordinary for WoW Classic. The game's previous experiment that many saw as a testing ground for Classic+, Season of Discovery, was announced at BlizzCon 2023 in early November and was then released only a few weeks later. It certainly seems like history could repeat for Classic+, Camelot, or whatever Blizzard officially calls it. But Classic+ is far from the only new Warcraft project included on the alleged leaked release slate. According to the alleged leak, Blizzard may also be making a new Warcraft RTS titled Warcraft Chronicles for 2027, as well as an Arthas RPG spin-off for 2028. Those would be huge news on their own, but beyond games, the leak additionally lists a tie-in television show for each game. The idea of Blizzard working on television shows isn't as far-fetched as it sounds. Faries said in an interview earlier this year Blizzard has had "exciting conversations" about Hollywood adaptations of its IP, while Blizzard VP and executive producer for WoW Holly Longdale has been on record that the Warcraft IP is "underutilized" and that Blizzard wants to expand it beyond just WoW. It's possible the leaked slate is years old and no longer accurate (or just an extremely coincidental fake), but it wouldn't be surprising if all of what it detailed and more appeared at BlizzCon. StarCraft Is Back In A Big Way StarCraft has been a largely dormant franchise for close to a decade. The last major DLC for StarCraft 2 released in 2017, the same year StarCraft: Remastered released. Since then, Blizzard's sci-fi franchise has been relegated to cosmetic crossovers in other Blizzard games like Diablo 4 and Hearthstone. That looks to be finally changing at BlizzCon this year. Persistent reports have indicated Blizzard is working on a StarCraft shooter of some kind, though additional details on what kind have been scarce. There are also reports Blizzard is partnering with Korean video game giant Nexon for a licensing deal that could potentially see Nexon develop new StarCraft games. At least one new StarCraft title getting revealed at BlizzCon this year seems like a certainty, though it's possible Blizzard also officially announces its partnership with Nexon as well. Blizzard is sending clear signals that something is happening on the StarCraft front . The website for StarCraft: Remastered recently started "glitching" out, perhaps serving as a not so subtle nod that news is on the way. Those "glitches" have revealed secret transmissions and bits of new lore that look to be setting the stage for Blizzard's shooter. Fans are theorizing the game could be a PvE co-op shooter in the vein of Helldivers 2, where a team of players land on an abandoned lunar mining facility overrun by Zerg, have to complete objectives, and then extract. Or it could be the triumphant return of StarCraft: Ghosts, though my money would be on the PvE co-op shooter. Regardless, StarCraft will almost certainly make a return at this year's BlizzCon, though its new form may disappoint RTS fans. Diablo New And Old What Blizzard is cooking up on the Diablo front is largely a mystery. It is, however, Diablo's 30th anniversary, so it seems safe to bet Blizzard will be announcing big news about the franchise at the show. A Diablo 30th anniversary presentation earlier this year concluded with Blizzard teasing a major BlizzCon announcement, stating "they are going to freak out at BlizzCon when we announce" a moment before the end of the broadcast. Alongside a Switch 2 port of Diablo 4 , the announcement of a new Diablo 4 expansion, alongside a reveal cinematic, is almost a given. Blizzard once pledged yearly expansions for Diablo 4. That didn't come to pass, but the gap between the game's Vessel of Hatred and Lord of Hatred expansion's was faster than Diablo fans are used to, with a little over a year and a half between them. With Lord of Hatred having been released back in April, a new expansion in the back half of 2027 seems plausible. Blizzard certainly has no shortage of villains to choose from, with Diablo himself having still failed to make an appearance in Diablo 4. The return of Malthael could also be in the cards, with the game's latest season making multiple not so subtle references to the fallen angel. Aside from a new expansion, Blizzard has already promised more details and surprises related to Season 15. Of course, Diablo as a franchise is bigger than Diablo 4. Earlier this year, Diablo 2: Resurrected received new content in the form of the Reign of the Warlock DLC , adding a new class and some long-requested quality-of-life features to the classic ARPG. There's also Diablo Immortal, the ongoing mobile game Blizzard co-operates with NetEase. A quick look at the BlizzCon schedule reveals there sure is a lot of time dedicated to a Diablo Immortal "event" across both days of the show, something fans are finding suspicious. It would certainly be bold of Blizzard to dedicate so much time and space to the game that led to the most memed moment in BlizzCon history, the infamous "do you guys not have phones?" moment from Diablo Immortal's reveal Q&A during BlizzCon 2018. That fact has led some fans to speculate that surely there must be something else related to Diablo coming that will take up more of that timeblock. The real question is what. It wouldn't be surprising if Blizzard announced a new Diablo 2 expansion. The demand clearly seems to be there given the reception to Reign of the Warlock, and there are still plenty of Diablo fans who view D2 as the pinnacle of the series in much the same way WoW Classic fans put vanilla WoW above all subsequent versions. Given it's the franchise's 30th anniversary, a potential remake of the original Diablo also seems like a possibility, though what form that might take is more uncertain. Overwatch Keeps Its Momentum Overwatch has had a big year so far, with Blizzard essentially rebooting its hero shooter by dropping the "2" from its name , putting an emphasis on year-long storylines, and adding more playable heroes this year than ever before. The game added five new heroes at once earlier this year, and has continued to add a new hero every season since. Going into BlizzCon 2026, I expect Blizzard to keep that momentum going into next year. By abandoning Overwatch 2's promised PvE story missions back in 2024 and even ceasing new content development for the game's newest game mode, Stadium , Blizzard looks to be focusing on what works and cutting out what doesn't. That's resulting in more events, cosmetics, crossovers, and heroes faster than ever, and Blizzard is no doubt putting more resources into ensuring that gravy train continues. As for what that means for BlizzCon, expect new map reveals and plenty of new hero announcements. Blizzard hasn't yet revealed the game's next hero coming as part of Season 5, so that's a shoo-in. There's a good chance a hero trial for the Season 5 hero goes live during BlizzCon, as was the case with Mauga's reveal at BlizzCon 2023. Season 6's new hero, and heroes even beyond that, will likely be revealed as well. Though Blizzard initially only promised a new hero for each 2026 season, I would be shocked if the new hero per season status quo doesn't continue into 2027. BlizzCon will also likely set the stage for the finale of Overwatch's 2026 storyline, The Reign of Talon. Story has been a big focus for Overwatch this year, with plenty of comics, short stories, and animations propelling the game's narrative forward. In addition to getting a good look at how 2026's storyline will conclude, I expect to learn where the story will be going next, too, with Blizzard possibly announcing the name and theme of 2027's seasonal story arc. One big question is whether Blizzard reveals a new core Overwatch game mode. Blizzard's track record hasn't been great on this front. Clash, added in 2024, hasn't been popular and was removed from both competitive and quickplay. Stadium was added last year, but its low player count saw Blizzard recently announce it was putting the mode on life support . I would be surprised then if Blizzard attempts to throw another new mode at the wall and see if it sticks so soon after Stadium's failure, as it seems like its resources would be better spent elsewhere. Rather than announcing a brand new mode, Blizzard may instead put more emphasis on 6v6. It's no secret Blizzard has been experimenting more and more with 6v6 in recent months. While I don't expect 5v5 to vanish, the introduction of a proper, permanent role queue for 6v6 seems like a real possibility. Whatever Blizzard is cooking across its franchises, fans won't have to wait long to learn what's in store. BlizzCon's opening ceremony begins September 12 at 10:30 AM PT / 1:30 PM ET.

title: Stop The Presses, Link Can Jump In Ocarina Of Time Remake
text: Today, Nintendo aired The Legend Of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct . We learned the Ocarina of Time remake is launching November 5 . We heard about a new orchestra concert touring the world in 2027 . We finally got to see the title of the upcoming full-length movie: The Legend Of Zelda (no, really, that's it) . Then, Eiji Aonuma walked us through a 15-minute gameplay demo of the upcoming Ocarina of Time Remake, and while the game's new look and gameplay are already being debated, there's no denying one crucial addition: Link can now jump on command. At one point, the younger version of Link comes across a pond with rocks that he must jump across. In the previous Ocarina of Time game, Link would automatically jump when approaching the rocks. Now, however, players can make Link jump whenever they like, at the press of a button. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PQvD3p2yGwc As Aonuma himself pointed out in the demo, jumping may not seem like a big deal, but because the original game didn't allow for free jumping, this is a major change in the context of Ocarina of Time. Though what was shown was faithful to the original, the combination of this jump mechanic and the new sprint mechanic could lead to some changes in level design in the final game. The gameplay demo also showed off the remake's updated visual style through multiple locations from the Nintendo 64 classic, including the Deku Tree, Hyrule Market, and Kokiri Forest. Aonuma also revealed new Ocarina mechanics, including the ability to hum a tune or play it on a physical instrument and have it register through the Switch 2's built-in microphone. The Ocarina of Time remake will borrow at least one mechanic from Breath of the Wild, as the ability to quickly swap between weapons was highlighted during the demo. The game will also feature full voice acting , which means Navi might be up for a redemption tour now that she can say more than "hey" and "listen." Finally, the rumored Zelda-themed Nintendo Switch 2 console was confirmed during the Direct, along with a Pro Controller, a carrying case, and new Amiibo figures of Young Link and Young Zelda. The console and Pro Controller will launch on October 29, one week before the remake releases, while the Amiibo will release in 2027.

title: The Legend Of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct Missed A Giant Wind Waker-Sized Opportunity
text: If you were hoping to see older Zelda games ported to or remastered for the Switch at the recent Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct , you were likely disappointed, as Nintendo instead dedicated almost the entire show to its upcoming Ocarina of Time remake. Out of all the Legend of Zelda remasters that have come to Switch consoles over the years, there's still a sizable Wind Waker HD-shaped hole in that collection. The Legend of Zelda: Wind Waker HD released on the Wii U in 2013, with a number of upgrades compared to the original 2003 GameCube version. While the original version of Wind Waker was added to the Switch Online GameCube library last year, the Wii U version is much better in comparison. It provides a smoother experience with various quality-of-life improvements, like a resolution boost, faster loading times, and subtle changes to the game that make it less of a chore to play in its second half. While it isn't considered as influential as Ocarina of Time, Wind Waker's impact can still be felt in modern Zelda games today. The fact then that the upgraded version of one of the best Zelda games of all time is still only available on the Wii U is a shame. Much the same could be said of Twilight Princess HD on the Wii U. Maybe I just had unrealistic expectations. For Zelda's 40th anniversary, I imagined Nintendo would do something similar to what it did for Mario's 35th anniversary, when it released Super Mario 3D All-Stars for a (baffingly) limited amount of time. The bundle put together three of Mario's greatest games in one package for the Switch, with updated 3D visuals, improved frame rates, and more. Is it unreasonable to expect Nintendo would do something along the same lines for Zelda, especially when the best versions of two of the franchise's greatest games are trapped in Wii U hell? Instead, we got a disappointingly limited direct that failed to even show a trailer for the franchise's upcoming live-action film adaptation. Nintendo certainly delivered on giving fans an in-depth look at Ocarina of Time's stunning remake. It looks fantastic and faithful to the original while still adding small, modern changes (like a jump button). I have no doubt the Ocarina of Time remake will be great when it releases November 5 . But if you wanted to see the best version of classics like Wind Waker and Twilight Princess receive new life on the Switch 2, it appears you'll have to keep waiting. Maybe Zelda's 50th anniversary will be a big enough ocassion.

title: The Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Remake Looks Fantastic In First Gameplay Look
text: After months of rumors, Nintendo finally revealed that The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake was real back in June. While that reveal was purely cinematic, today's Nintendo Direct for The Legend of Zelda showed off gameplay for the remake and offered a closer look at its updated art direction. The Switch 2 exclusive stays true to the 1998 original's aesthetics, while showcasing a huge upgrade visually. Link's hat and tunic, for example, showcase detailed threading and embroidering, along with berries on his cap. The lighting system looks fantastic, too, as sunlight pokes through the forest as Link heads to the Great Deku Tree. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PQvD3p2yGwc As for gameplay, players will have a button for Link to jump and dash. That may sound silly to younger people who grew up on The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom, but it's a huge change from the Nintendo 64 title. How the jump button could possibly impact dungeon design wasn't addressed but should prove interesting later this year. Overall, the first gameplay revealed for The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake seemed to address a lot of my concerns of a simple remaster for the game . The Switch 2 title seems faithful while still altering enough for modern audiences--and those of us who played the original (or 3DS remaster) plenty of times already. Long considered to be the greatest Legend of Zelda game--until the Switch era at least, thanks to Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom--Ocarina of Time was originally released for the Nintendo 64 console. The first 3D Zelda game, Ocarina of Time, was a trailblazer and laid the foundation that future entries in the franchise would emulate. The game has received multiple ports and remasters over the years, and out of all of them, the 3DS version is considered the best of the best thanks to the various quality-of-life changes added to the game--including some welcome revisions to the Water Dungeon. title: Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Remake Borrows At Least One Mechanic From Breath Of The Wild
text: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on Switch 2 looks like a very faithful remake of the Nintendo 64 classic, but as seen in the Zelda 40th anniversary Direct , this updated version of the game takes at least one element from the modern open-world Zelda games. When demonstrating the returning Fairy Slingshot item, Zelda producer Eiji Aonuma showed off the weapon-switching and aiming mechanics, which look nearly identical to the same systems in Breath of the Wild. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PQvD3p2yGwc Players can quickly swap their weapons in a horizontal menu similar to the one used in Breath of the Wild, Tears of the Kingdom, and Echoes of Wisdom. Aiming a projectile weapon also uses the same reticle seen in Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom, with full motion control support as well. The difference in Ocarina is that you can use Z-targeting in conjunction with free aim. Upon the official announcement of the Ocarina of Time remake, speculation amongst the Zelda fanbase ran rampant about whether the new title would remain faithful to the original game or reimagine it to be similar to modern Zelda titles. While Aonuma made it clear from the beginning of his presentation that Nintendo is taking the former approach, it looks like there will at least be some UI and quality-of-life elements taken from recent games. In terms of significant changes made in the remake, there's a major difference in how time passes compared to the original game. Link can also manually jump in the remake, a contrast to his auto-jumping in the 1998 original. The Zelda Direct revealed that the Ocarina of Time remake launches on November 5 , a stone's throw away from Grand Theft Auto 6. Nintendo also announced that the live-action Zelda movie is simply titled "The Legend of Zelda," and a 40th anniversary concert tour will take place in 2027.

title: Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Remake Release Date Is November 5, Just Before GTA 6
text: As part of the Zelda-themed Nintendo Direct today , Nintendo announced that The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time's new remake for Switch 2 will release on November 5. What's more, Nintendo is promising "snappier and more satisfying" action, faster load times, and a "much smoother" experience overall. There are new run and jump mechanics, too, and improved camera controls. Additionally, characters that Link meets on his journey are "fully voiced" in what Nintendo says are "expanded cutscenes." The game's day/night cycle is back in the remake, but now the cycle applies to wherever players are, including in towns. What's more, the Ocarina of Time remake allows players to hum songs in real life, with the sounds then transposed into the game for Link to perform. Nintendo will also sell a real ocarina that players can use. Ocarina of Time was originally released in 1998 for the Nintendo 64, and it's one of the most beloved entries in the series. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PQvD3p2yGwc 2026 is the 40th anniversary of the Zelda franchise. title: The Legend Of Zelda Movie, Based On The Legend Of Zelda, Is Called The Legend Of Zelda
text: After teasing fans with a few images earlier this year, Nintendo finally gave a little more info about the Legend of Zelda live-action movie . Very little! We now have a final title, but Nintendo chose not to share any additional images or a trailer yet. The movie will release on April 30, 2027. Series creator Shigeru Miyamoto appeared briefly to share that the final title is simply The Legend of Zelda. He called attention to the lack of subtitle, and said that once you see the movie the simplicity of the title will make sense. The movie stars Bo Bragason (Zelda) and Benjamin Evan Ainsworth (Link). "Once you've seen the film, you'll understand why there isn't a subtitle," Miyamoto said. "This is an original film based on the many stories, ideas, and concepts of the series, built up through the years for 40 years. Through the creative power and visual expertise of the talented production team, it's become an artistic work worthy of the Legend of Zelda series." Directed by Wes Ball (Kingdom of the Planet of the Apes), this is the first live-action movie based on a Nintendo property since the infamous Super Mario Bros. flick from 1993. Ball has previously mentioned that he's aiming to bring Studio Ghibli aesthetics to this adaptation, as well as a sense of realism to the fantasy adventure. Filming for the Zelda movie began in November 2025 in New Zealand--the same country where Peter Jackson shot his legendary Lord of the Rings trilogy--and production wrapped in April 2026. The Legend of Zelda movie will hit theaters in May 2027.

title: EA Used AI To Clone John Buccigross’ Voice In NHL 27
text: Electronic Arts utilizes generative AI systems in its suite of development tools, and now another example has come to light. John Buccigross, the ESPN personality who joined the in-game broadcast booth for NHL 27 this year, has revealed that EA Sports used generative AI to simulate his voice in some scenarios. The developers seemingly did not disclose this prior to launch. He said on the Chirping Zebras podcast ( via 23sabres ) that the developers played some AI-produced lines back for him, and he said they were "pretty good." However, he also recalled times when the AI tools didn't get things completely right, so a human had to make corrections. He said in one scenario, the AI voice said, "And the crowd gets out of the chairs." In ice hockey, though, a commentator in reality would not say "chairs" but instead "seats." At the end of the day, Buccigross sounded pretty enthusiastic about the AI features in NHL 27. "If it means less work and the same check, I'll take it," he said. EA Sports previously used generative AI to help with its popular College Football series. The developers said the game would not have been as good without it . EA CEO Andrew Wilson is a big believer in utilizing AI to help make games faster and more efficiently, even if it means job losses and displacement in the short term. Wilson said EA conducted a study across all of its development processes and found that 60% of development processes have a “high feasibility” of being positively impacted by generative AI. As an example, Wilson said in the past it took six months to develop a stadium for one of its sports games, and now it takes six weeks. In the future, it could take six days, he said. EA’s ambition, Wilson said, is to use generative AI to make its development processes 30% more efficient. Wilson said EA’s development teams are driven by the desire to “get to the fun faster” and release games faster. The aim is to “get to greatness much more quickly,” he said. EA was recently sold to an investor consortium led by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF). The deal came with billions in debt for EA, so many are expecting the company to enact mass layoffs, game cancellations, studio closures, and other cost-cutting efforts, though no specific restructuring plan has been confirmed at this stage.

title: Resident Evil Director Says He Won’t Do A Franchise Movie Again
text: Director Zach Cregger is making one of 2026's most-anticipated video game movies in Resident Evil , but don't expect him to make another film based on a franchise again. Speaking to Deadline , Cregger said, "I'm doing this [Resident Evil], and that's it for me. I'm not going to go tackle any other franchises." Why? He said it's because he wants to "write whatever I want to write," as opposed to adhering to a specific franchise's history and lore. "I don’t want to write something where I have to make sure I’m tagging different data points to satisfy X. I just want to satisfy me," he said. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mNd1gb19A-c Cregger said the "only reason" that Resident Evil made sense for him was because he's a big fan of the games and he came up with what he believes is an original idea for it. "I think this movie is cool, and I hope it checks the fan boxes because I’m a fan and I’m checking my boxes. I’m making the Resident Evil movie that I wish existed, so I can do that with a clean heart and a clear conscience and not feel like I’m getting f*cked by some weird industry thing," he said. Cregger also clarified comments he made previously about his story for the Resident Evil movie. Some had theorized that what Cregger meant when he said he came up with an original story for Resident Evil was that he wrote a story and then slapped the Resident Evil name on it. That's not quite the case. "What I mean is it’s an original story, but it’s still a Resident Evil story. I’m not taking a story from the games; that’s what that means," he said. Something else that might have convinced Cregger to sign on to write and direct Resident Evil was the money--he was reported to have been paid $20 million . While Cregger may be finished with franchise movies, he is attached to co-write the upcoming Siren Head movie . Cregger's next movie is The Flood, a sci-fi movie set in deep space. Resident Evil releases in theaters on September 18, and it's expected to have the biggest opening weekend ever for the movie series .

title: Rumored 3D Mario Game Could Finally Be Revealed At Tomorrow’s Nintendo Direct

title: Capcom Is Getting My Hopes Up For Devil May Cry 6 With Its Talk Of “Reactivating” Dormant Franchises
text: A new Onimusha game hit PC and consoles last week, and so far, it looks like Capcom has yet another win on its hands. Onimusha: Way of the Sword sold 1 million copies on launch day--bringing lifetime sales for the franchise up to 10 million--which is pretty impressive for a series that has been dormant for the better part of 20 years. Commenting on the early sales milestone, Capcom said that it wants to repeat Onimusha's success with other games that haven't seen a new release in many years. "In addition to regularly releasing major new titles each year, Capcom is focusing on reactivating IPs that haven't had a new title launch recently," Capcom wrote in a statement. "The company is working to further maximize corporate value by leveraging its rich library of content, including this title." https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I2sSPdSPvCU Capcom added that "several marketing initiatives," alongside demos and hands-on exhibitions, also helped spread awareness of the new Onimusha, helping to drive sales. It also helps that the game is genuinely good , with gorgeous visuals and exciting combat that keeps you on the edge of your seat. As for which games could make the cut, take your pick. I'd argue that Devil May Cry is due a fresh sequel, considering that the last game, Devil May Cry 5 , was released in 2019, but Lost Planet, Viewtiful Joe, and Dino Crisis fans might fervently disagree with me--and those are just a few of the games that have been gathering dust at Capcom over the years. Whatever Capcom does decide to reactivate, it'll land in the wake of a very successful 2026 for the company. Things got off to a hot start with the release of Resident Evil Requiem in February, and the momentum increased with the launch of Monster Hunter Stories 3: Twisted Reflection in March and the sleeper hit Pragmata in April. On top of that, several Capcom games like Street Fighter 6 have continued to enjoy post-launch support, and future releases include Dragon's Dogma 2: Dark Arisen in October, a major expansion for Monster Hunter Wilds, and Resident Evil Veronica . We're even getting a first taste of Capcom's reactivation strategy next year, with the launch of Mega Man: Dual Override .
